shouldFix.title: The artifact's self-description is stale on both limbs, and the obligation its purpose promises to name is not named
shouldFix.finding: Two problems in one place. First, authorityClaim is byte-identical to v1's and says the artifact states 'which existing condition-4 gate owns each class, and which classes need a later D-086 named harness.' The body now denies both limbs: no existing gate owns any class, and a D-086 named harness is precisely what the artifact says will not satisfy gate 3. An artifact whose authorityClaim contradicts its own content on both counts misdescribes itself to anyone who reads that field first, and it is the field a coordinator entry would quote. Second, purpose says 'Name the later DR-G* obligation those classes require', but proposedObligation names nothing: it has kind, notPerformedHere, notABareD086Identifier, doesNotAddTheRowHere, doesNotAmendD002Here and ownsAllSevenNTs, and no id, no claim text, and no owner. 'A later DR-G* obligation, its own D-000 cycle' is a category, not a name. The artifact is elsewhere precise about the difference between naming and not naming — that precision is the substance of its B2 repair — so the loose reading of 'name' sits badly with its own vocabulary. The gap matters because the withdrawal of the G10 joins leaves the specification of that future obligation as this artifact's remaining contribution, and ownsAllSevenNTs asserts one obligation covers protocol-frame refusal, fact admission, host policy, Coverage-domain sufficiency, D9 minting and planAdmission without proposing a claim that spans them.
shouldFix.whyNotBlocker: Nothing asserted about the seven classes is false, and the gate-3 statement that replaced v1's dead route is correct. This is a self-description and specification gap in a candidate that binds nothing.
shouldFix.repair: Rewrite authorityClaim to match the body: the artifact states that no live DR-G* cell owns any of v3's NT-1..NT-7 as written, and characterises the later DR-G* obligation those classes require. Then either propose that obligation concretely — a candidate gate id, a claim sentence covering host-owned admission, and a candidate owner, all marked proposed-not-adopted the way v1 marked its harness id — or change purpose to say the artifact characterises rather than names it. If one obligation is really to own all seven, the proposed claim should be the demonstration of that.

shouldFix.title: The universal negative that now carries the whole artifact is argued against one gate out of twenty-two
shouldFix.finding: purpose asserts that 'none of v3's NT-1..NT-7 is owned by a live DR-G* cell as written', and every class records existingGate 'none'. The only reasoning offered is whyNotG10 on each class, which points at g10DoesNotOwn, which addresses DR-G10 alone. Twenty-one other live gate claims are neither quoted nor mentioned. That negative is not a side remark: it is what justifies creating a new DR-G* obligation, and adding a required gate is a D-002 required-gate-set change, which is among the heavier acts in this corpus. The nearest neighbours deserve a sentence each rather than silence — DR-G09 PERMISSIONS 'Requested/granted/denied and enforced/disclosed outcomes are truthful' sits near NT-4's waiver and threshold limb, and DR-G21 COMPONENT-FAILURE-CONTAINMENT 'One component failure never crashes the core or leaks uncommitted authority' sits near NT-4 and NT-7's authority limbs. I checked all 22 claims myself and the conclusion holds: neither of those owns a component asserting authority on a well-formed path, and no other gate owns host-side fact or policy admission. So this is a reviewability defect, not a wrong answer — but the next reviewer, and the D-000 cycle that would create the new gate, should not have to redo the scan to find that out.
shouldFix.whyNotBlocker: The conclusion is correct on independent measurement, so nothing false is being recorded. What is missing is the basis.
shouldFix.repair: Add a short surveyedGates block: the 22 gate ids with the claim text of the two or three nearest neighbours, and one line each on why they do not own these classes. That converts the artifact's central claim from an assertion into something a later cycle can check without repeating the work.

independence.otherReviewerHandling: A Codex v1 verdict exists and a Codex v2 file may follow; neither was opened. The prompt states Codex accepted v1 at 0/0, and I take that from the prompt rather than from the file.
independence.priorPosition: I rejected v1 at 2 blockers and 1 SHOULD-FIX. v2 accepts all three findings, which is the situation where a reviewer is most likely to wave the successor through. Every repair was therefore re-verified against primary sources — the live DR-G10 row field by field, D-056's gate 3 in the pinned turn-2 subject, v3's negative tests, and a fresh read of all 22 gate claims — rather than against the artifact's own disposition table.
independence.notEscalated: I did not raise the absence of a proposed gate claim as a blocker, nor demand that the artifact perform the DR-G* naming act; that act is expressly a later D-000 cycle and D-002 question, and requiring it here would contradict the very finding v2 accepted.

coordinatorSummary: REJECT at 0 blockers and 3 SHOULD-FIX. Fifteen attacks run, three landed, none of them a blocker. This is a substantial improvement and all three of my v1 findings land in full, verified against primary sources rather than the artifact's own disposition table: the three DR-G10 joins are withdrawn and G10 is now characterised strictly within its quoted cells, with NT-6 handled by exactly the distinction I drew between a component-minted D9 refusal and G10's fault-join golden; the dead identifier-only route is replaced by a correct statement of D-056 gate 3; and all eight DR-G10 cells are now quoted, nine of nine quotations byte-exact against the live row, with Status 'HARD-BLOCKED pending selector refresh' and the 'any semantic change needs successor' waiver both restored. Custody is clean — 138787be at 0444 unmoved, v1 frozen at a69926b6 with its own prompt still retrievable at its own path, HEAD never left 2d1254e — and the seven classes still match v3 name for name. Three gaps remain, all repairable and none of them a false statement. First, the artifact misdescribes itself: authorityClaim is byte-identical to v1's and still says the artifact states which existing gate owns each class and which classes need a D-086 named harness, both of which the body now denies, while purpose promises to 'Name the later DR-G* obligation' and proposedObligation names nothing — no id, no claim, no owner — even as it asserts one obligation owns all seven classes. Second, the universal negative that now carries the whole artifact, that no live DR-G* cell owns any of the seven, is argued against one gate out of twenty-two; that negative is what would justify creating a new required gate, a D-002-set change, and the nearest neighbours DR-G09 and DR-G21 deserve a sentence each. I read all 22 claims myself and the conclusion is correct, so this is reviewability rather than error — but the next cycle should not have to redo the scan. Third, the rewrite dropped the pin to provider-only-output-contract.v3: neither its path nor its digest ef2a7416 appears anywhere in v2, though the artifact is entirely a map of that contract's retained classes. The transcription is faithful, which is what keeps it at SHOULD-FIX. A v3 that fixes the self-description, records the gate survey, and restores the source pin would keep everything listed under whatSurvives and, on what I can measure, would accept.
